skills.name: Andika sentensi ukiacha nafasi ifaayo kati ya maneno
skills.mastery: Writes sentences with one finger space between words, none inside a word, keeps the verb and its parts as one word (ninakwenda, not ni na kwenda) and does not run on into the next sentence, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also checks it in the exercise book).

prerequisites.reason: Neat letters on the line come before spacing the words.
Writing single words properly in Grade 1.

misconceptions.error: Leaves no space between words (Basilimefika).
misconceptions.cause: Speech runs words together and the child writes the stream as he hears it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Basilimefikamapema." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Put a finger space after each word; count the words aloud first.
misconceptions.feedback: Acha nafasi ya kidole kati ya neno na neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits the verb into its parts (ni na kwenda, a li fika).
misconceptions.cause: The child hears the parts of the verb as separate sounds and writes a space after each.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Mimi ni na kwenda sokoni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the whole verb in one line; it is one word however long.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendo ni neno moja: ninakwenda.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts a space inside a word at a syllable (ba si, ga ri).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt to write syllable by syllable and leaves a gap after each.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Ga ri ni jekundu." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Write the syllables close together and read the word aloud; then the gap goes after the word.
misconceptions.feedback: Silabi za neno moja hukaa pamoja: gari.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves very large gaps between some words and none between others.

example.question: Nafasi kati ya maneno inafaa kuwa vipi?

misconceptions.cause: The child does not measure; he writes as space allows on the line.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Nafasi kati ya maneno inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "yoyote, kubwa au ndogo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Use a finger or a lolly stick as the measure for each gap.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila nafasi iwe sawa na kidole kimoja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Soma na uandike vifungu vya maneno ya usafiri katika umoja na wingi
skills.mastery: Reads and writes word groups about transport in singular and plural: li-ma nouns take ma- (basi - mabasi, gari - magari), people take wa- (mwendeshaji - waendeshaji), n-n nouns stay the same (ndege - ndege) and the describing word agrees, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Two-word groups in the plural (Theme 2) come first.
Singular and plural of nouns (Grade 1).

misconceptions.error: Makes the plural with the prefix of another noun class (kitabu -> watabu).
misconceptions.cause: The child knows that wa- makes people plural and uses it for everything; the ngeli of the noun is not yet known.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "mwendeshaji" ni?" with "miendeshaji" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Sort noun cards into ngeli families (m-wa, ki-vi, li-ma, n-n) and say each plural aloud.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila ngeli ina wingi wake: kitabu - vitabu, mtoto - watoto. (waendeshaji)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives a noun of the n-n class a plural prefix (nyumba -> manyumba), or changes an irregular noun wrongly (jicho -> majicho).
misconceptions.cause: The child expects every plural to look different; n-n nouns stay the same and some li-ma nouns change their stem.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "ndege moja" ni?" with "mandege mawili" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a short list of the same-in-both nouns (nyumba, ndizi, kalamu) and the irregular ones (jicho - macho, jino - meno).
misconceptions.feedback: Baadhi ya nomino hazibadiliki, na baadhi hubadilika kwa njia yake. (ndege mbili)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Shows the plural only with a number word and leaves the noun singular (kitabu mbili).
misconceptions.cause: English and some first languages keep the noun and add a number; Kiswahili changes the noun and the number agrees.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "gari moja" ni?" with "gari mbili" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Line up two books: the child says vitabu viwili; then three: vitabu vitatu.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino hubadilika pia: vitabu viwili. (magari mawili)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Takes the plural form for the singular (miti for one tree, vitabu for one book).
misconceptions.cause: The child heard the plural more often (a tree is usually among trees) and learnt it as the name.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi liko katika umoja?" with "magari" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold one object, then many; the child names each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kimoja ni kitabu; vingi ni vitabu. (gari)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves the adjective singular with a plural noun (watoto mzuri).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun only.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "basi kubwa" ni?" with "mabasi kubwa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Change the noun to many and ask the child to change every word that goes with it.
misconceptions.feedback: Watoto wazuri: vyote hubadilika. (mabasi makubwa)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Sikiliza kifungu, eleza ujumbe na msamiati wake, na usimulie upya
skills.mastery: After hearing a short passage (Sungura mjanja alimdanganya fisi akaokoa chakula chake), says its message, gives the meaning of a new word from it, uses the word in a sentence of his own and retells the events in order, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Listening to a short story and answering about it in Grade 1 comes first.
Finding the message of a read passage is the same work as for a heard one.

misconceptions.error: Gives a detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ulichosikiliza ni upi?

misconceptions.cause: The detail is the clearest thing the child remembers; he has not been asked what the passage teaches.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ulichosikiliza ni upi?" with "Sungura alikuwa na chakula." among the options.
misconceptions.help: After listening, ask "Kifungu kinatufundisha nini?" and compare it with "Nini kilitokea?".
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Akili hutusaidia kujiokoa tukiwa hatarini.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives "mjanja" the meaning of a word that sounds like it.

example.question: Neno "mjanja" katika kifungu lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the sound of the word to one he knows instead of listening to the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "mjanja" katika kifungu lina maana gani?" with "mjinga" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Replay the sentence; the child tries each meaning in it and keeps the one that makes sense.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "mjanja" ni mwenye akili ya kutafuta njia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Makes a "sentence" that only repeats the word and shows no meaning (mjanja ni mjanja).

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi inaonyesha maana ya "mjanja"?
example.correct_answer: Sungura mjanja alitafuta njia ya kumtoroka fisi.

misconceptions.cause: The child thinks any sentence with the word in it is enough.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni sentensi ipi inaonyesha maana ya "mjanja"?" with "Mjanja ni mjanja." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: if your friend did not know the word, would your sentence tell him what it means?
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi nzuri inaonyesha maana ya neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells the events out of order.

example.question: Panga matukio ya kifungu kama yalivyotokea.
example.wrong_answer: Sungura alitoroka, fisi alimkuta sungura, sungura alimdanganya fisi
example.correct_answer: Fisi alimkuta sungura, sungura alimdanganya fisi, sungura akatoroka

misconceptions.cause: The child remembers the most exciting event and tells it first.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Panga matukio ya kifungu kama yalivyotokea." with "Sungura alitoroka, fisi alimkuta sungura, sungura alimdanganya fisi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Three picture cards of the events; the child lays them left to right and retells with kwanza, kisha, mwishowe.
misconceptions.feedback: Matukio yalifuatana hivi: Fisi alimkuta sungura, sungura alimdanganya fisi, sungura akatoroka.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Adds events that were not in the passage when retelling.

example.question: Unaposimulia upya, unaongeza mambo ambayo hayakuwa kwenye kifungu?

misconceptions.cause: Retelling is taken as storytelling: the child invents to make it longer.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposimulia upya, unaongeza mambo ambayo hayakuwa kwenye kifungu?" with "ndiyo, ili hadithi iwe tamu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: After the retelling, the class checks each event: was it in the passage? Thumbs up or down.
misconceptions.feedback: Kusimulia upya ni kusema yaliyokuwa kwenye kifungu tu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

key_inquiry_questions: Je, ni mambo gani yanayokusaidia kupata ujumbe kwenye vifungu vya ufahamu?

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi: msamiati, ujumbe, kutabiri na mafunzo
skills.mastery: Reads a short passage on mnyama nimpendaye, gives the meaning of a theme word from the sentence around it, says the message, predicts what happens next from the clues in the picture and says the lesson, answering from the passage and not from his own life, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The comprehension questions of Theme 3 come first.
Answering about a short read passage in Grade 1.

misconceptions.error: Gives "hulinda" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Kiprono ana mbwa anayeitwa Simba. Kila siku humpa chakula na maji. Usiku, Simba hulinda nyumba dhidi ya wezi." Neno "hulinda" lina maana gani?

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Soma: "Kiprono ana mbwa anayeitwa Simba. Kila siku humpa chakula na maji. Usiku, Simba hulinda nyumba dhidi ya wezi." Neno "hulinda" lina maana gani?" with "hulima" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "hulinda" ni huangalia ili pasiwe na hatari.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.
misconceptions.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Mbwa anaitwa Simba." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Tukiwatunza wanyama wetu, nao hutusaidia.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Predicts something the passage gives no clue for, without looking at the picture.

example.question: Picha inaonyesha mtu asiyejulikana langoni usiku. Simba atafanya nini?

misconceptions.cause: Prediction is taken as free imagination; the child has not been shown that clues in the text and picture point the way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Picha inaonyesha mtu asiyejulikana langoni usiku. Simba atafanya nini?" with "Atalala." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the clue words and point at the picture; the guess must fit them.
misconceptions.feedback: Tabiri kwa kutumia dalili za picha na za kifungu: Atabweka ili kuwaamsha watu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells what happened when asked for the lesson.
misconceptions.cause: The lesson question sounds like a what-happened question to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?" with "Kiprono humpa mbwa maji." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Start the answer with "Tunajifunza kwamba tunapaswa..."
misconceptions.feedback: Funzo ni: Tunapaswa kuwatunza wanyama wetu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mbwa wa Kiprono anaitwa nani?" with "Mbwa wetu anaitwa Bobi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu liko kwenye kifungu: Simba
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tumia alama ya kiulizi ipasavyo katika maandishi
skills.mastery: Tells a question from a statement, ends each with its mark (? or .), starts the next sentence with a capital, and writes a passage of about 20 words with the marks in place, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Ending a sentence with a kikomo (Grade 1) comes before the kiulizi.
A capital follows the mark.

misconceptions.error: Ends a question with a kikomo.
misconceptions.cause: The child ends every sentence the same way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Weka alama sahihi: Unaenda wapi" with "Unaenda wapi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the sentence aloud: if the voice rises and asks, it takes a kiulizi.
misconceptions.feedback: Swali huishia kwa kiulizi (?).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts a kiulizi after a statement.

example.question: Weka alama sahihi: Mimi ninaenda sokoni

misconceptions.cause: The child uses ? as a decoration or thinks any sentence about himself is a question.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Weka alama sahihi: Mimi ninaenda sokoni" with "Mimi ninaenda sokoni?" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask: does the sentence want an answer? If not, kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi ya kueleza huishia kwa kikomo (.).
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts a kiulizi after a reported question (Mama aliniuliza ninaenda wapi?).

example.question: Weka alama sahihi: Mama aliniuliza ninaenda wapi

misconceptions.cause: The question word wapi makes the child think the sentence is a question; it only tells that one was asked.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Weka alama sahihi: Mama aliniuliza ninaenda wapi" with "Mama aliniuliza ninaenda wapi?" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Compare "Unaenda wapi?" (asked now) with "Aliniuliza ninaenda wapi." (told).
misconceptions.feedback: Sentensi hii inaeleza kwamba swali liliulizwa; huishia kwa kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts several kiulizi (???) for a strong question.
misconceptions.cause: Text messages and cartoons use many marks; the child copies them.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Je, sungura anakula nini???" among the options.
misconceptions.help: One question, one kiulizi; show a page from the class reader.
misconceptions.feedback: Swali moja, kiulizi kimoja.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a small letter after a kikomo or kiulizi.
misconceptions.cause: The child does not link the mark to the capital that follows it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Sungura anakula majani. mama alifurahi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Every kikomo is a gate: the next word starts big.
misconceptions.feedback: Baada ya kikomo, herufi kubwa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kusilikiliza kifungu au wimbo unaohusu matumizi ya –ako na –enu katika kifaa cha kidijitali,
kutambua matumizi ya -ako na -enu katika kadi za maneno, mti maneno, kapu maneno na vifaa halisi kwa kusaidiwa na mwalimu,
kumtungia mwenzake sentensi zenye matumizi ya -ako na –enu,
kusikiliza sentensi zinazotungwa na wenzake zenye matumizi ya -ako na -enu na kuzitolea maoni,
kuwasilisha sentensi zenye kutumia maneno -ako na –enu,
kuandika sentensi zenye -ako na –enu,
kujaza nafasi kwa kutumia -ako na -enu kwa kusaidiwa na mwalimu.
key_inquiry_questions: Je,-ako na - enu hutumiwa wakati gani?

Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika kumtungia mwenzake sentensi akitumia –ako na -enu.

Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapotunga sentensi sahihi akitumia -ako na -enu kwa lugha fasaha.

Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapojitolea kumtungia mwenzake sentensi akitumia –ako na -enu.

Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kutoka maeneo tofauti tofauti kutunga sentensi zenye matumizi yafaayo ya -ako na –enu akizingatia mada lengwa.
Elimu ya utunzaji wa wanyama: mwanafunzi anapotunga sentensi kuhusu mnyama nimpendaye.

Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya matumizi ya -ako na -enu anayojifunza katika somo la Kiswahili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.
Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha suala la mnyama nimpendaye na suala la Evironmental Activities.

kutumia -ako na - enu ipasavyo katika sentensi

skills.name: Tumia -ako na -enu ipasavyo katika sentensi
skills.mastery: Uses -ako for something owned by one person spoken to and -enu for many, with the prefix of the thing owned (mbwa wako, vikombe vyako, madaftari yenu), placed after the noun, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: -angu and -etu (Grade 1) show the owner pattern.
Wewe and nyinyi (Theme 1) are the owners of -ako and -enu.

misconceptions.error: Uses the wrong noun-class form of the possessive (kitabu yangu for kitabu changu).
misconceptions.cause: Town Kiswahili uses yangu, yako, yake for every noun; the child has not seen the ngeli agreement.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Mbwa ___ (-ako) ni mkubwa." with "yako" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pair nouns and possessives by colour: kitabu changu, kiti chake, mtoto wangu.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitabu changu; kiti chake: kimilikishi hufuata ngeli. (wako)
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves the possessive singular with a plural noun (vitabu changu).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun and forgets the possessive.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Vikombe ___ (-ako) ni safi." with "chako" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Change one object to many in front of the child; both words change.
misconceptions.feedback: Vitabu vyangu: vyote viwili hubadilika. (vyako)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the possessive of the wrong owner (-ake for something that is his own, -ake for many owners).
misconceptions.cause: The child has not linked -angu, -ako, -ake, -etu, -enu, -ao to who owns the thing.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anawaambia wanafunzi wote: "Leteni madaftari ___."" with "yako" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold up an object: Ni cha nani? Answer with the owner first, then the possessive.
misconceptions.feedback: Mwenye kitu ni nani? Mimi: changu; yeye: chake; wao: chao. (yenu)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the possessive before the noun (yangu kalamu), in English word order.
misconceptions.cause: English puts "my" before the noun; Kiswahili puts it after.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "wako paka" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Build the phrase with cards: the noun first, then the possessive.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino kwanza, kimilikishi baadaye: kalamu yangu. (paka wako)
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tambua na utamke silabi za sauti /ny/, /ng/ katika maneno na sentensi
skills.mastery: Hears and says the target sounds /ny/, /ng/ in syllables and words (nyanya, ngoma, nyama), splits a word into its syllables, and picks or uses a word that carries the sound, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Splitting words into syllables comes before ny and ng.
Hearing target syllables in Grade 1.

misconceptions.error: Says /n/ for /ny/, so "nyanya" becomes "nanya".

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "nyanya". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

misconceptions.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /ny/, or do not separate it from /n/; the child puts in the home sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "nyanya". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "nanya" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza: "nyanya" ina sauti /ny/, si /n/.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Pushes a vowel into the cluster, so "nyota" is said "niyota".
misconceptions.cause: In the child's first language, or in English loan habits, two consonants rarely sit together; he breaks them with a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tamka neno "nyota". Ni lipi sahihi?" with "niyota" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say the cluster in one beat, then the word; clap once for the cluster syllable.
misconceptions.feedback: "nyota" ina silabi nyo-ta; hakuna irabu ya ziada.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops part of the target sound, so "ngoma" becomes "goma".

example.question: Neno "ngoma" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?

misconceptions.cause: The second part of the sound (the w or y glide, or the soft nasal) is quick and quiet; the child does not hear it and leaves it out.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "ngoma" limeandikwa au kutamkwa vipi kwa usahihi?" with "goma" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stretch the syllable slowly (p-y-a), then say it fast; the child copies.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza tena: "ngoma". Usiache sehemu ya sauti.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Splits "nyanya" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
misconceptions.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "nyanya" lina silabi zipi?" with "n-y-a-n-y-a" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
misconceptions.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: nya-nya.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /ny/, /ng/?" with "baba" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
misconceptions.feedback: "ngoma" ina sauti lengwa; "baba" haina.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua sauti lengwa katika kifungu chepesi kuhusu suala lengwa akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kuhusu suala lengwa kwa kuzingatia matamshi bora akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa sauti inayosikika akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia kasi ifaayo (maneno 39 kwa dakika na kwa kuizingatia viakifishi) akishirikiana na wenzake,
kusoma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti lengwa kwa kuzingatia ishara zifaazo akishirikiana na wenzake kuhusu suala lengwa,
kusoma hadithi kutoka kwenye kitabu, kifaa cha kidijtali akishirikirikiana wenzake akizingatia sauti inayosikika, matamshi bora, kasi ifaayo na ishara zifaazo kuhusu suala lengwa,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi kifungu chepesi chenye sauti lengwa akizingatia matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara zifaazo.

Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kutambua sauti lengwa na kusoma kifungu kwa ufasaha.

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi chenye sauti /ny/, /ng/ kwa matamshi bora, sauti inayosikika, kasi ifaayo na ishara
skills.mastery: Finds the target sounds /ny/, /ng/ in a short story, reads it aloud with every sound clear, loud enough for the class, at about 39 words a minute, pausing at the koma and kikomo and raising the voice for a question; in the app picks the better reading of a line, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Saying ny and ng comes before reading them aloud.
Reading short sentences aloud in Grade 1.

misconceptions.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "nyumba" as "numba".
misconceptions.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Neno "nyumba" linasomwa vipi?" with "numba" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma "nyumba" kama lilivyoandikwa.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Babu na bibi wanaishi kijijini."?

misconceptions.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Babu na bibi wanaishi kijijini."?" with "Babu ... na ... bibi ... wanaishi ... kijijini." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

misconceptions.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 39 kwa dakika

misconceptions.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
misconceptions.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, umemtembelea nyanya?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

misconceptions.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, umemtembelea nyanya?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
misconceptions.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Andika maneno yanayotamkwa kwenye imla kwa tahajia sahihi
skills.mastery: Writes the words the teacher reads (about 10 words) with the right letters: the Kiswahili sound and not the home sound, the nasal kept (nd, mb, ng), long vowels doubled and ng' with its apostrophe, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Hearing ny and ng clearly comes before writing family words from dictation.
Writing two-syllable words from dictation in Grade 1.

misconceptions.error: Spells the word with the sound of his first language: "shangazi" written "sangazi".
misconceptions.cause: The child writes as he says the word; if his first language merges the two sounds, the letter is a guess.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "sangazi" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Keep a list of the class's hard pairs (l/r, s/sh, z/dh, s/th); say each word slowly before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Andika "shangazi" kama linavyotamkwa kwa Kiswahili sanifu.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Drops the nasal: "ndugu" written "dugu".
misconceptions.cause: The n or m before a consonant is soft and quick; the child does not hear it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "dugu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hum the nasal before the word (mmm-bwa, nnn-dege).
misconceptions.feedback: "ndugu" lina sauti ya pua mwanzoni.
misconceptions.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes a long vowel short, so the word changes: "kaa" written "ka".

example.question: Andika neno lenye maana ya "kuketi au kuishi mahali".

misconceptions.cause: The child hears the length but does not know it is shown by two letters.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Andika neno lenye maana ya "kuketi au kuishi mahali"." with "ka" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Clap the two vowels as two beats; compare a word with one and two vowels.
misconceptions.feedback: "kaa" lina irabu mbili zinazofuatana.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Writes ng' without the apostrophe (ngombe for ng'ombe), or puts it where it does not belong (ng'oma for ngoma).

example.question: Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?

misconceptions.cause: Ng' and ng are two sounds; the apostrophe looks like dirt on the page to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?" with "ngombe" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Say ng'ombe and ngoma: the first has no g sound; mark it with the apostrophe.
misconceptions.feedback: Ng'ombe huandikwa na kibainishi: ng'.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Joins two words into one, or splits one word into two (kwasababu; mwana funzi).
misconceptions.cause: In speech the words run together; the child has not seen each written apart.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Nilichelewa kwasababu ya mvua." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Count the words aloud with a finger for each before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: "Kwa sababu" ni maneno mawili.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

skills.name: Tumia -refu, -kubwa na -tamu ipasavyo katika sentensi
skills.mastery: Uses -refu, -kubwa and -tamu after the noun with the right prefix (babu mrefu, kiti kikubwa, nyumba ndefu, wajomba warefu) and picks the right member of a pair (mrefu or mfupi), in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The ngeli and plural of two-word groups come before adjective agreement.
-zuri and -baya (Grade 1) are the first adjectives that agree.

misconceptions.error: Gives the adjective the people prefix whatever the noun (kiti mzuri).
misconceptions.cause: Mzuri is the form the child hears most (mtoto mzuri) and is used everywhere.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kiti ___ (-kubwa)." with "mkubwa" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Match noun and adjective by colour: kiti kizuri, mtoto mzuri, vitu vizuri.
misconceptions.feedback: Kivumishi hufuata ngeli: kiti kizuri. (kikubwa)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives an n-n noun the m- form of the adjective (nyumba mzuri for nyumba nzuri).
misconceptions.cause: The n- prefix and its sound changes (nzuri, ndefu, nyeupe) are new to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Nyumba ___ (-refu)." with "mrefu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read pairs aloud: nyumba nzuri, kalamu ndefu, nguo nyeupe.
misconceptions.feedback: Nyumba nzuri; nguo nyeupe. (ndefu)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Puts the adjective before the noun (mzuri mtoto), in English word order.
misconceptions.cause: English puts the describing word first.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "mrefu babu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Build with cards: noun first, then the adjective.
misconceptions.feedback: Nomino kwanza: mtoto mzuri. (babu mrefu)
misconceptions.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Leaves the adjective singular with a plural noun (watoto mzuri).
misconceptions.cause: The child changes the noun only.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Jaza: Wajomba ___ (-refu)." with "mrefu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Change the noun to many and ask the child to change every word that goes with it.
misconceptions.feedback: Watoto wazuri: vyote hubadilika. (warefu)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Picks the opposite member of the pair (mrefu for a short person).

example.question: Picha inaonyesha mti mfupi. Mti ni ___.

misconceptions.cause: The pair is learnt together and the two words are swapped.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Picha inaonyesha mti mfupi. Mti ni ___." with "mrefu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Act the pairs with the body: stretch for refu, crouch for fupi.
misconceptions.feedback: Angalia picha tena na uchague neno linalofaa. (mfupi)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua maagizo ya hatua mbili,
kutazama video ya jinsi ya kutoa na kufuata maagizo mepesi ya hatua mbili kwa kifaa cha kidijitali kuhusu suala lengwa,
kushiriki katika kutoa na kufuata maagizo mepesi ya hatua mbili,
kufafanua umuhimu wa maagizo,
kuimba nyimbo na kukariri mashairi yanayohusu maagizo kuhusu suala lengwa.
key_inquiry_questions: Kufuata maagizo kuna umuhimu gani?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika mjadala na wenzake wakati wa ujifunzaji katika kikundi.
Uwazaji kwa kina na utatuzi wa matatizo: mwanafunzi anapotoa na kufuata maagizo kulingana na yanavyotolewa.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunzia.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki kuimba nyimbo na pia kukariri mashairi kuhusu maagizo.
sub_strands.values:
Amani: mwanafunzi anapofanya maigizo katika kikundi na wenzake kwa utulivu.
Haki za kijamii: mwanafunzi anapomtolea mwenzake maagizo yafaayo.
Umoja: mwanafunzi anapofanya kazi na wenzake katika kikundi kwa upole na kuelewana.
sub_strands.pcis:
Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kutazama video ya jinsi ya kutoa na kufuata maagizo ya hatua mbili kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali kuhusu suala lengwa.
Utunzi na usalama wa watoto: mwanafunzi anaposikiliza vifungu kuhusu sebuleni na vifaa vya sebuleni.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha stadi ya kufuata maagizo anayojifunza katika somo la Kiswahili na ujifunzaji wa stadi hiyo katika somo la English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua maagizo mepesi ya hatua mbili yanapotolewa katika miktadha mbalimbali
kutoa na kufuata maagizo mepesi ya hatua mbili yanayotumiwa katika miktadha mbalimbali
kuchangamkia maagizo katika maisha ya kila siku

skills.name: Fuata na utoe maagizo mepesi kwa usahihi
skills.mastery: Follows a one- or two-step instruction in the right order, reads the direction and action words in it (simama, keti, kulia, kushoto, juu, chini), and gives a clear, polite instruction that names what to do and to what, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Following one-step instructions in Grade 1 comes before two steps.
A polite instruction uses tafadhali.

misconceptions.error: Carries out only the first part of a two-step instruction.

example.question: Agizo: "Panga viti, kisha ufagie sebule." Umefanya nini?

misconceptions.cause: The child starts acting as soon as he hears the first verb and stops listening.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Agizo: "Panga viti, kisha ufagie sebule." Umefanya nini?" with "anapanga viti tu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Hold up one finger for each step while giving the instruction; the child repeats the steps before moving.
misconceptions.feedback: Sikiliza agizo lote kwanza, kisha fanya hatua zote.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Does the steps in the wrong order.

example.question: Agizo: "Osha mikono, kisha ule chakula." Ni nini kinatangulia?

misconceptions.cause: The child does the step he wants most first; the order words kwanza and kisha are not yet noticed.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Agizo: "Osha mikono, kisha ule chakula." Ni nini kinatangulia?" with "kula chakula" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Number the steps on the board with kwanza, kisha, mwishowe.
misconceptions.feedback: Neno "kisha" linaonyesha hatua inayofuata.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Mixes a direction or action word.

example.question: Agizo: "Weka kikombe juu ya meza." Ni kitendo kipi sahihi?

misconceptions.cause: Pairs such as kulia/kushoto and juu/chini are learnt together and swapped.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Agizo: "Weka kikombe juu ya meza." Ni kitendo kipi sahihi?" with "anakiweka chini ya meza" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Play "Mwalimu anasema": the teacher calls the word, the child acts it; mark the right hand with a band.
misconceptions.feedback: Weka kikombe juu ya meza. maana yake ni anakiweka juu ya meza.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives an instruction that leaves out what to act on, or with no polite word (Lete!).

example.question: Ni agizo lipi liko wazi na lina adabu?

misconceptions.cause: The child knows what he means and does not see that the listener cannot.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ni agizo lipi liko wazi na lina adabu?" with "Lete!" among the options.
misconceptions.help: The child gives the instruction to a partner, who does exactly what was said and no more.
misconceptions.feedback: Agizo zuri linasema nini kifanyike, kwa kitu gani, na kwa adabu.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kusoma kifungu chepesi cha maneno 43-46 na kutambua msamiati wa suala lengwa ( runinga, kochi, meza,radio ) akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutabiri kitakachotokea katika hadithi akizingatia picha kwenye kifungu akishirikiana na wenzake,
kutabiri ujumbe wa kifungu kwa kutazama picha kwenye kitabu, vifaa vya kidijitali au chati akishirikiana na wenzake kuhusu suala lengwa,
kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu akishirikiana na wenzake,
kuthibitisha utabiri wake kuhusu hadithi baada ya kuisoma.
kutumia msamiati wa suala lengwa ipasavyo katika mawasiliano.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, tunawezaje kupata ujumbe katika ufahamu?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi na kuchangia kikamilifu.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapotumia vifaa vya kidijitali kujifunzia.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapomtajia mzazi au mlezi vitu vinavyopatikana sebuleni mwao kwa kutumia msamiati aliojifunza.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapowaheshimu wenzake wanapotangamana katika shughuli za kikundi.
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kwa upendo katika shughuli mbalimbali za kikundi.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anapoeleza wenzake kuhusu vitu vya sebuleni.
sub_strands.pcis:
Elimu ya afya ya kujikinga: mwanafunzi anaposoma kifungu chepesi na kutambua msamiati wa wa swala lengwa kama zulia, kochi, viti na jinsi ya kuviweka safi ili kuweza kujikinga na maradhi.
Haki za watoto: mwanafunzi anaposoma ufahamu kuhusu sebuleni na vifaa vya sebuleni.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha stadi ya kusoma kwa ufasaha anayojifunza katika somo la Kiswahili na ujifunzaji wa stadi hiyo katika somo la English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua msamiati kuhusu suala lengwa katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kutabiri yatakayotokea katika kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu kwa kuzingatia picha
kueleza ujumbe wa kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu
kueleza mafunzo yanayotokana na kifungu chepesi cha ufahamu

skills.name: Soma kifungu chepesi: msamiati, ujumbe, kutabiri na mafunzo
skills.mastery: Reads a short passage on sebuleni, gives the meaning of a theme word from the sentence around it, says the message, predicts what happens next from the clues in the picture and says the lesson, answering from the passage and not from his own life, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: The comprehension questions of Theme 5 come first.
Answering about a short read passage in Grade 1.

misconceptions.error: Gives "sakafu" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Sebuleni kwetu kuna viti vinne, meza na runinga. Kila Jumamosi, mimi na dada yangu hupangusa vumbi na kufagia sakafu. Sebule huwa safi na nadhifu." Neno "sakafu" lina maana gani?
example.correct_answer: sehemu ya chini ya chumba tunayoikanyaga

misconceptions.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Soma: "Sebuleni kwetu kuna viti vinne, meza na runinga. Kila Jumamosi, mimi na dada yangu hupangusa vumbi na kufagia sakafu. Sebule huwa safi na nadhifu." Neno "sakafu" lina maana gani?" with "safari" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika kifungu, "sakafu" ni sehemu ya chini ya chumba tunayoikanyaga.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.
misconceptions.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Kuna viti vinne." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
misconceptions.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Tushirikiane kuweka nyumba yetu safi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Predicts something the passage gives no clue for, without looking at the picture.

example.question: Picha inaonyesha wageni wakibisha mlango. Watoto watafanya nini?

misconceptions.cause: Prediction is taken as free imagination; the child has not been shown that clues in the text and picture point the way.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Picha inaonyesha wageni wakibisha mlango. Watoto watafanya nini?" with "Watajificha." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Underline the clue words and point at the picture; the guess must fit them.
misconceptions.feedback: Tabiri kwa kutumia dalili za picha na za kifungu: Watawakaribisha wageni sebuleni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Retells what happened when asked for the lesson.
misconceptions.cause: The lesson question sounds like a what-happened question to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Tunajifunza nini kutokana na kifungu?" with "Kuna runinga sebuleni." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Start the answer with "Tunajifunza kwamba tunapaswa..."
misconceptions.feedback: Funzo ni: Tunapaswa kusaidia kazi za nyumbani.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
misconceptions.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Watoto husafisha sebule siku gani?" with "Sisi husafisha Jumapili." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
misconceptions.feedback: Jibu liko kwenye kifungu: Jumamosi
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua vipengele vya kuhariri katika maandishi kwenye kitabu, chati au kifaa cha kidijitali akishirikiana na wenzake,
kuandika kifungu cha maneno mawili au sentensi fupi daftarini au kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali,
kujadiliana na wenzake kuhusu vipengele vya kuzingatia katika uhariri,
kuipitia kazi yake baada ya kuiandika ili kuhariri tahajia, nafasi baina ya sauti na maneno pamoja na viakifishi kuhusu suala lengwa,
kushirikiana na wenzake kuhariri kazi aliyoandika,
kumwonyesha mzazi au mlezi kifungu alichohariri ili ampe maoni yake.
key_inquiry_questions: Je, kwa nini ni vizuri kusoma kazi uliyoandika na kuirekebisha?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuwaonyesha wenzake nafasi baina ya maneno katika kifungu cha maneno mawili au sentensi fupi.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuandika kifungu cha maneno mawili au sentensi fupi akitumia kifaa cha kidijitali.
Hamu ya ujifunzaji: mwanafunzi anapofaulu kuhariri kifungu cha maneno mawili au sentensi fupi akizingatia nafasi ipasavyo.
sub_strands.values:
Upendo: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake na kuheshimu maoni yao.
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapowatambua na kuwathamini wenzake wakati wa kushiriki katika shughuli ya kuhariri kifungu cha maneno mawili na sentensi fupi.
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kazi ya kikundi.
sub_strands.pcis:
Mshikamano wa kijamii: mwanafunzi anapoandika kifungu kifupi kuhusu shughuli zinazofanywa na familia yao wanapojumuika sebuleni.
Haki za watoto: mwanafunzi anapoandika kifungu kuhusu sebuleni na vifaa vya sebuleni.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha stadi ya kuhariri anayojifunza katika somo la Kiswahili na ujifunzaji wa stadi hiyo katika somo la English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua vipengele vya kuhariri katika maandishi
kuhariri maandishi yake baada ya kuyaandika
kufurahia kuhariri maandishi baada ya kuyaandika ili kuimarisha mawasiliano

skills.name: Hariri maandishi yako: herufi kubwa, kikomo, maneno na tahajia
skills.mastery: Reads his own writing back and corrects it: a capital at the start, a kikomo or kiulizi at the end, no word left out, words spelt right, then makes a clean copy, in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also checks the before and after copies).

prerequisites.reason: Knowing where the marks go comes before checking for them.
Knowing where the capitals go comes before checking for them.
Spelling words of Grade 1 correctly.

misconceptions.error: Thinks editing means copying the same writing more neatly, mistakes and all.
misconceptions.cause: The child has seen clean copies praised and thinks neatness is the whole job.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kuhariri ni nini?" with "kuandika upya kwa mwandiko mzuri" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Give a short passage with three planted mistakes; the child finds them before copying.
misconceptions.feedback: Kuhariri ni kutafuta na kusahihisha makosa.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Does not read his writing back, so a missing word stays missing.

example.question: Sahihisha: Mama alipika chakula kitamu sana sana.
example.wrong_answer: Mama alipika chakula kitamu sana sana.

misconceptions.cause: The child knows what he meant and his eye fills the gap or skips the repeat.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Sahihisha: Mama alipika chakula kitamu sana sana." with "Mama alipika chakula kitamu sana sana." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Read it aloud with a finger under each word.
misconceptions.feedback: Soma kwa sauti, neno kwa neno.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Checks spelling only and leaves out the capital and the kikomo.
misconceptions.cause: Spelling is what the teacher marks most, so it is all the child looks for.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Hariri: tuliketi sebuleni" with "tuliketi sebuleni" among the options.
misconceptions.help: An editing card: Herufi kubwa? Kikomo? Neno limekosekana? Tahajia?
misconceptions.feedback: Angalia herufi kubwa mwanzoni na kikomo mwishoni.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Rubs out so hard the page tears, or scribbles over the error so it cannot be read.

example.question: Ukipata kosa, unafanya nini?
example.wrong_answer: ninalifuta kwa nguvu au kulichora juu
example.correct_answer: ninapiga mstari mmoja juu yake na kuandika sahihi

misconceptions.cause: The child fears a mistake showing.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Ukipata kosa, unafanya nini?" with "ninalifuta kwa nguvu au kulichora juu" among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show one neat line through the error and the right word above it.
misconceptions.feedback: Piga mstari mmoja juu ya kosa, andika sahihi.
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

sub_strands.sub_strand: Ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili, umoja na wingi (Theme 7: Sebuleni)
learning_experiences: kutambua ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili, umoja na wingi, katika kadi maneno, mti maneno kuhusu suala lengwa,
kusikiliza kifungu au wimbo kuhusu ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili umoja na wingi kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali,
kushirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kukanusha sentensi katika nafsi ya pili, umoja na wingi kuhusu suala lengwa, kwa mfano: wewe - ulisoma – wewe hukusoma,
kutunga sentensi zinazoashiria ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili umoja na wingi kuhusu suala lengwa kwa kusaidiwa na mwalimu,
kufanya zoezi la kujaza nafasi kwa kutumia nafsi ya pili, umoja na wingi, kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali,
kumsomea mzazi au mlezi sentensi alizokanusha katika nafsi ya pili, umoja na wingi ili ampe maoni.
key_inquiry_questions: Ukanushaji wa sentensi katika umoja na wingi unahusu nini?
sub_strands.core_competences:
Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki kumtungia mwenzake sentensi katika kikundi kwa kutumia nafsi ya pili umoja na wingi.
Kujiamini: mwanafunzi anapoigiza vitendo vinavyoashiria nafsi ya pili umoja na wingi.
Ujuzi wa kidijitali: mwanafunzi anaposikiliza kifungu au wimbo kuhusu ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili umoja na wingi kwenye kifaa cha kidijitali.
Ubunifu: mwanafunzi anapotunga sentensi zinazoashiria ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili umoja na wingi.
sub_strands.values:
Heshima: mwanafunzi anapoheshimu mchango wa wenzake wanapotungiana sentensi kwenye kikundi kwa kutumia ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili umoja na wingi.
Uwajibikaji: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake katika kikundi kukanusha sentensi zilizo katika nafsi ya pili umoja na wingi.
Umoja: mwanafunzi anaposhiriki katika shughuli za kikundi.
sub_strands.pcis:
Usalama mtandaoni: mwanafunzi anapofanya shughuli ya ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili katika umoja na wingi kuhusu suala lengwa akizingatia hatua za kiusalama katika mtandao.
Utunzi na usalama watoto: mwanafunzi anapoandika sentensi kuhusu suala lengwa.
sub_strands.links: Mwanafunzi anaweza kuhusisha dhana ya nafsi anayojifunza katika somo la Kiswahili na ujifunzaji wa dhana hiyo katika somo la English Language Activities na Indigenous Language Activities.

outcomes.text: kutambua ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili, umoja na wingi katika sentensi
kutumia ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili, umoja na wingi katika sentensi kwa usahihi
kuchangamkia matumizi ya ukanusho wa nafsi ya pili, umoja na wingi, katika mawasiliano ya kila siku

skills.name: Kanusha sentensi za nafsi ya pili umoja na wingi
skills.mastery: Makes the negative of a present-tense sentence in the second person: wewe unasoma - wewe husomi, nyinyi mnasoma - nyinyi hamsomi (hu-/ham-, no -na-, final -a to -i), in 8 of 10 new items (the teacher also hears it in class, with the KICD rubric).

prerequisites.reason: Wewe/nyinyi and their subject markers come before their negatives.
Negating a simple sentence in Grade 1.

misconceptions.error: Keeps the final -a in the negative present (hasoma for hasomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child adds the negative prefix and leaves the rest of the verb as it was.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Wewe unasoma." with "Wewe husoma." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show the pair with the end of the verb circled: anasoma - hasomi.
misconceptions.feedback: Katika ukanushaji wa wakati uliopo, -a inakuwa -i: hasomi. (Wewe husomi.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Keeps the tense marker -na- in the negative (hanasomi for hasomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child negates by adding ha- to the whole positive verb.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Wewe unapika." with "Wewe hunapiki." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Cross out na in the positive form and change the end.
misconceptions.feedback: Hasomi: hakuna -na- katika ukanushaji huu. (Wewe hupiki.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Negates by putting si before the positive verb (Yeye si anasoma).
misconceptions.cause: Si is the negative the child knows (si mimi), so he puts it in front of any sentence.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Nyinyi mnasoma." with "Nyinyi si mnasoma." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Show si as the negative of ni (Yeye si mwalimu) and ha- as the negative of a verb.
misconceptions.feedback: Kitendo hukanushwa kwa ha-: Yeye hasomi. (Nyinyi hamsomi.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

misconceptions.error: Uses the negative prefix of another person (Wao hasomi for hawasomi; Mimi hasomi for sisomi).
misconceptions.cause: The child learnt one negative form (ha-) and uses it for all persons.
misconceptions.reveals: The question "Kanusha: Nyinyi mnacheza." with "Nyinyi hawachezi." among the options.
misconceptions.help: Table of persons: si-, hu-, ha-, hatu-, ham-, hawa-; the child points before writing.
misconceptions.feedback: Wao hawasomi; mimi sisomi. (Nyinyi hamchezi.)
misconceptions.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

learning_experiences: kutambua silabi za sauti lengwa katika matini mbalimbali kama vile kadi maneno, chati, mti maneno, au kifaa cha kidijitali,
kusikiliza maneno yenye silabi za sauti lengwa yakitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali,
kutamka maneno aliyosikiliza pamoja na mwalimu na mwishowe kutamka akishirikiana na wenzake kuhusu suala lengwa,
kusikiliza kwa makini sentensi zenye sauti lengwa na zinazolenga suala lengwa zikitamkwa na mwalimu, mgeni mwalikwa au kifaa cha kidijitali na kuzitambua,
kusikiliza na kusimulia kifungu cha hadithi kuhusu suala lengwa (k.v usalama wangu na jinsi ya kudumisha usalama barabaran),
kujirekodi akisoma hadithi zilizo na maneno na sentensi zenye sauti lengwa na kujisikiliza na wenzake ili kutathmini matamshi bora.
key_inquiry_questions: Unajua kutamka maneno gani yenye sauti /sh/ na /th/?

Mawasiliano na ushirikiano: mwanafunzi anaposhirikiana na wenzake kutambua na kutamka maneno yenye sauti lengwa.
